subject: Phase 100180 — Audit Trail, Inspect, and Correction (staged diff, 48 non-workflow files)
verdict_justification: All ten findings were addressed with evidence. issues.title: Pre-existing SQLite databases never receive the new lineage columns
issues.why_it_matters: A schema change shipped without an upgrade path for the default in-process backend silently breaks correct/audit_trail on any existing SQLite file.
issues.impact: correct_item/audit_trail SQL references items.corrects_item_id/superseded_by_id; a v6 SQLite DB lacks them and fails at runtime with 'no such column'. Only Postgres converges.

issues.proposed_fix: Bump schema_version and add a SQLite convergence path (guarded ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, or extend sqlite_items_stale to detect missing columns).

findings.title: make coverage is not reliably green (flaky shared-Postgres index test)
findings.evidence: First `make coverage` run (2026-09-19) failed: `index_store_tests::tests::postgres_index_contract` panicked at crates/clio-store/src/index_store_tests.rs:239 'backoff is lifted when the cutoff is None'; exit 101. It passes in isolation (cargo test -p clio-store --lib index_store: 4 passed) and 5/5 plain full-lib runs, and 2 of 3 subsequent `make coverage` runs. The assertion reads the whole store via `pending_index_jobs(10, None)` (crates/clio-store/src/postgres_index.rs:243-249, ORDER BY queued_at LIMIT 10); the phase's new pg tests add index_pending rows in the shared DB, saturating the first-10 window under coverage instrumentation.
findings.recommendation: Scope the assertion to the test's own bank (e.g. a bank-filtered pending query) or raise/removal of the global limit; do not claim a reliably green coverage gate until it passes repeatedly.
findings.resolution: Resolved by evidence: the shared-store `pending_index_jobs` assertions in the index contract now read a 1_000_000-row window, so this test's own bank rows cannot be displaced by unrelated queued rows from parallel tests. Production global LIMIT semantics are unchanged (the worker legitimately pulls jobs across banks).
findings.resolution_evidence: crates/clio-store/src/index_store_tests.rs (`ALL_PENDING = 1_000_000`); index_store suite 4/4 passed in `make check`; `make coverage` exited 0 with postgres_index_contract green.

findings.title: Required scenario T100180-04 (as_of historical query) is never tested
findings.evidence: Phase 100180 §8 T100180-04 requires: 'Query historical fact via as_of after correction | Returns original value at past timestamp'. No test in the staged diff uses as_of/time_axis for items (grep for as_of/time_axis in audit_correct_tests.rs, pg_audit_tests.rs, correct_reject_tests.rs, clio-compliance tests: 0 hits). Tests only re-read the prior row directly and assert tx_until/valid_until + snapshot (crates/clio-store/src/audit_correct_tests.rs:167-200, crates/clio-compliance/src/correct_tests.rs:199-225). The capability to test it exists: clio-retrieve/src/filter.rs:40 item_visible_at() honours TimeAxis for items.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that calls retrieve/compose with as_of before and after the correction on time_axis=transaction and asserts the old then new value; or correct the AC wording if row-level inspection is intended.
findings.resolution: Added the T100180-04 test at the bi-temporal visibility layer over the rows the correction actually wrote: `t18_04_as_of_transaction_returns_prior_then_corrected_value` asserts `item_visible_at(TimeAxis::Transaction)` selects the original revision before the correction and the corrected revision after, and that the prior keeps its original value. Recommendation adjusted with evidence: the hybrid lexical/dense legs index only live rows (`items.tx_until IS NULL`), so `retrieve`/`compose` cannot surface a superseded revision; transaction-axis item history is surfaced by `audit_trail` plus this predicate. AC-100180-04 wording was corrected to say exactly that.
findings.resolution_evidence: crates/clio-retrieve/src/audit_asof_tests.rs; crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_index.rs lexical leg `items.tx_until IS NULL`; phase AC-100180-04 + Known Limitations.

findings.title: inspect does not return a total count, so T100180-06 is unmet
findings.evidence: Phase 100180 §8 T100180-06 requires 'Exactly limit items returned with accurate total count'. The inspect payload is {items, limit, offset, include_discarded} only (crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs:206-211); Store::inspect_items returns Vec<ItemInspectRow> with no count (crates/clio-store/src/store.rs:313). No test asserts a total. AC-100180-03 marks inspect filtering PASS without mentioning total.
findings.recommendation: Add a count query (same predicates, no limit/offset) and return `total`; assert it in the pagination test. If total is intentionally out of scope, say so and downgrade T100180-06.
findings.resolution: Added `Store::count_items` (same predicate compiler, no limit/offset) and returned `total` in the MCP inspect payload; asserted in unit, binding, Postgres-parity, and stdio tests.
findings.resolution_evidence: crates/clio-store/src/store.rs; sqlite_inspect.rs / postgres_inspect.rs `count_items_impl`; crates/clio-mcp/src/read_tools.rs; read_tools_tests.rs, audit_tools_tests.rs, pg_inspect_tests.rs, mcp_audit_conformance.rs.

findings.title: Pre-existing SQLite databases never receive the new lineage columns
findings.evidence: sql/001_core.sql:146-147 adds items.corrects_item_id/superseded_by_id for fresh DBs; sql/002_vectors_postgres.sql:35-36 converges pre-existing Postgres DBs via ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS. sql/002_vectors_sqlite.sql has no equivalent ALTER (grep 'ALTER TABLE' sql/: only 002_vectors_postgres.sql). schema_version stays '6' (crates/clio-store/src/schema_reshape.rs:26) and sqlite_items_stale() only checks class/epistemic_kind (schema_reshape.rs:29-58), so a v6 SQLite DB is not reshaped. correct_item/audit_trail SQL references the missing columns and fails at runtime with 'no such column'.
findings.requirement_ref: Phase 100180 Task 1/Task 4; Must-Not-Change in-process schemas; FR-16
findings.recommendation: Bump schema_version and add a SQLite convergence path (ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN guarded by table_info, or extend sqlite_items_stale to detect the missing columns) so existing SQLite DBs upgrade.
findings.resolution: Added SQLite schema convergence: `schema_converge::converge_lineage_columns_sqlite` runs before portable DDL and adds missing lineage columns via guarded `ALTER TABLE` (SQLite has no ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS). The lineage index creation moved out of portable 001 into the per-dialect 002 files so a legacy database is never indexed before its columns exist; this also fixes the equivalent Postgres ordering hazard, where 001's indexes ran before 002's ALTER. `schema_version` bumped 6 -> 7.
findings.resolution_evidence: crates/clio-store/src/schema_converge.rs; crates/clio-store/src/sqlite.rs (convergence call); sql/001_core.sql, sql/002_vectors_sqlite.sql, sql/002_vectors_postgres.sql; schema_converge_tests.rs (3 tests).

findings.title: Continuous corrections emit no `correct` telemetry and are invisible to audit_trail
findings.evidence: The continuous branch writes operation='continuous_observe' with item_id=NULL (crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_attribute.rs:283-295; postgres_attribute.rs same). AC-100180-01 claims a 'correct' row on correction, but no 'correct' event exists for the continuous path, and audit_trail(item_id) cannot return it (no attribute-key anchor: sqlite_audit.rs:55-72 returns ItemNotFound). The Known Limitations entry (phase file line 489) says such corrections are 'auditable through the same-transaction continuous_observe telemetry row', but no exposed tool lists audit_events rows.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-15, §4.12, phase-100180 Task 4 ('Emit a telemetry record with operation: correct')
findings.recommendation: Either label the continuous-correction audit row operation='correct' (with attr_key in detail) and expose an attribute-key audit view, or state plainly in the limitation that continuous corrections are not surfaced by audit_trail (not 'auditable').
findings.resolution: Reasoned continuous observations now persist `operation: correct` (with `attr_key` and reason in the detail); plain observations stay `continuous_observe`. The Known Limitations entry was reworded to state plainly that continuous corrections are NOT surfaced by item-level `audit_trail` (no attribute-key audit view is exposed), instead of calling them 'auditable'.

findings.title: MCP correct dry-run (confirm=false) does not validate a non-empty reason
findings.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/mutator_tools.rs:145-172 returns the would_correct preview after only req_str('item_id'/'reason') presence checks; a blank-string reason with confirm omitted succeeds. The blank-reason rejection only fires on the confirmed path (audit_tools_tests.rs:123-136 uses confirm=true). Security acceptance says 'Calling correct without a reason returns a 400-class error'.
findings.recommendation: Validate reason (and target existence) before returning the preview so the dry-run and confirmed paths agree.
findings.resolution: The MCP `correct` handler now rejects a blank/whitespace reason before returning the dry-run preview, matching the confirmed path (target existence remains checked on confirm; the preview writes nothing).
findings.resolution_evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/mutator_tools.rs; audit_tools_tests::correct_dry_run_then_confirm_supersedes asserts the preview fails with `invalid_argument`.

findings.title: inspect time_range upper bound is inclusive, not half-open [start,end)
findings.evidence: Phase 100180 Task 3 specifies time_range [start, end). inspect_query.rs:95-103 compiles created_at >= start and created_at <= end (inclusive). Pre-existing, unchanged by this phase; AC-100180-03 claims time-range filtering is covered.
findings.recommendation: Change the upper bound to `<` (or document the inclusive choice) and add a boundary test.
findings.resolution: Changed the inspect time_range upper bound to exclusive (`created_at < end`) per Task 3's half-open `[start, end)`; updated the filter docs and compiler test, and added a boundary assertion on both backends.

findings.title: audit_trail returns three parallel arrays, not the consolidated timeline AC evidence describes
findings.evidence: AC-100180-02 evidence says audit_trail 'merges revision rows + telemetry events + belief confidence trajectory, ordered ascending'. AuditTrailView exposes separate revisions/events/belief_confidence arrays (crates/clio-compliance/src/audit.rs:37-48), each sorted independently; Task 2's Expected Result ('an ordered array of every change') is not a single merged sequence.
findings.recommendation: Either interleave revisions+events into one timeline array or reword the evidence to say the arrays are individually ordered.
findings.resolution: AuditTrailView now returns a single merged `timeline` array (revisions + telemetry events + belief points) ordered ascending by `(timestamp, kind, id)`, in addition to the three individually ordered arrays; it is secret-masked like the rest.
findings.resolution_evidence: crates/clio-compliance/src/audit.rs; audit_tests timeline tests; mcp_audit_conformance.rs asserts timeline ordering over stdio.
